declared.title: Unpacking the pursuit of happiness: Being concerned about happiness but not aspiring to happiness is linked with negative meta-emotions and worse well-being
declared.foundIn: docs/design/review-science.md ; titre relevé par le relecteur science sur Crossref (contrôle d'identité plus faible pour cette fiche)

population: students and community adults, diverse in gender, ethnicity, age and place (N = 1,815)

findings.text: Judging and worrying about one's happiness, not wanting to be happy, goes with lower well-being

support.sentence: In Study 2, concern about happiness (but not aspiring to happiness) was associated with lower well-being cross-sectionally and longitudinally.

findings.text: That link runs partly through feeling bad about one's feelings during good moments

support.sentence: In Study 3, these links between concern about happiness and worse well-being were partially accounted for by experiencing greater negative meta-emotions during daily positive events.

limits: same network of authors as Ford 2018 and Mauss 2011
about judging one's happiness, not about judging one's negative emotions (blind review)
